    // APPROXIMATE. The circumference of an ellipse is a complete elliptic integral
    // of the second kind and has NO elementary closed form; this is RAMANUJAN'S
    // SECOND APPROXIMATION,
    //     P ~= pi (a + b) (1 + 3h / (10 + sqrt(4 - 3h))),  h = ((a-b)/(a+b))^2,
    // which is exact for a circle (h = 0) and degrades monotonically with
    // eccentricity: the worst case is the fully degenerate ellipse b = 0, where it
    // returns (14/11)*pi*a = 3.99838*a against the true 4*a — a relative error of
    // -4.0e-4. MEASURED against a converged arc-length integral, the relative error
    // is -4.6e-10 at b/a = 0.5, -6.3e-9 at b/a = 0.4, -7.4e-8 at b/a = 0.3,
    // -1.2e-5 at b/a = 0.1 and -3.8e-4 at b/a = 0.001. So "below 1e-8" holds only
    // for b/a >= 0.4; do not assume this body is accurate for flattened ellipses.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellipse#Circumference
    Perimeter(e: Ellipse): Number
    {
        var a = e.SemiAxes.X;
        var b = e.SemiAxes.Y;
        var h = ((a - b) / (a + b)).Square;
        return Number.Pi * (a + b) * (1.0 + 3.0 * h / (10.0 + (4.0 - 3.0 * h).Sqrt));
    }

    // The centre, by the ellipse's point symmetry.
    Centroid(e: Ellipse): Point2D
        => e.Center;

    // TIGHT bounds for a rotated ellipse: the half-extents are
    // sqrt(a^2 cos^2 phi + b^2 sin^2 phi) and sqrt(a^2 sin^2 phi + b^2 cos^2 phi),
    // the support of the ellipse along each world axis.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellipse#General_ellipse
    Bounds(e: Ellipse): Bounds2D
    {
        var c = e.Rotation.Cos;
        var s = e.Rotation.Sin;
        var dx = ((e.SemiAxes.X * c).Square + (e.SemiAxes.Y * s).Square).Sqrt;
        var dy = ((e.SemiAxes.X * s).Square + (e.SemiAxes.Y * c).Square).Sqrt;
        return CenteredBounds(e.Center, dx, dy);
    }

    // True when (x/a)^2 + (y/b)^2 <= 1 in the ellipse's own frame. Boundary
    // inclusive.
    Contains(e: Ellipse, point: Point2D): Boolean
    {
        var q = LocalOffset(e.Center, e.Rotation, point);
        return (q.X / e.SemiAxes.X).Square + (q.Y / e.SemiAxes.Y).Square <= 1.0;
    }

    //==
    // # SuperEllipse
    //
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superellipse


    // CONSERVATIVE, not tight: the world-axis-aligned box of the ROTATED local
    // bounding rectangle [-a, a] x [-b, b], which contains the superellipse for
    // every exponent. Tight only at Exponent -> infinity (the rectangle itself);
    // at Exponent = 2 the tight box is the ellipse formula above, which is smaller.
    // TODO(content): the tight support function of a superellipse is
    // a*|cos t|^(2/n) style and is not attempted here.
    Bounds(se: SuperEllipse): Bounds2D
    {
        var c = se.Rotation.Cos.Abs;
        var s = se.Rotation.Sin.Abs;
        return CenteredBounds(se.Center,
            se.SemiAxes.X * c + se.SemiAxes.Y * s,
            se.SemiAxes.X * s + se.SemiAxes.Y * c);
    }

    // True when |x/a|^n + |y/b|^n <= 1 in the superellipse's own frame — the
    // defining Lame inequality. Boundary inclusive.
    Contains(se: SuperEllipse, point: Point2D): Boolean
    {
        var q = LocalOffset(se.Center, se.Rotation, point);
        return (q.X / se.SemiAxes.X).Abs.Pow(se.Exponent)
            + (q.Y / se.SemiAxes.Y).Abs.Pow(se.Exponent) <= 1.0;
    }

    // The superellipse area: 4*a*b*Gamma(1 + 1/n)^2 / Gamma(1 + 2/n), via the
    // `Gamma` of `numbers.library.plato` (~1e-12 relative). Exact
    // in form: n = 2 gives pi*a*b (the ellipse), n -> infinity tends to 4*a*b
    // (the rectangle). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superellipse#Mathematical_features
    Area(se: SuperEllipse): Number
        => 4.0 * se.SemiAxes.X * se.SemiAxes.Y
         * Gamma(1.0 + 1.0 / se.Exponent).Square
         / Gamma(1.0 + 2.0 / se.Exponent);

    // The arc-length integrand of the local-frame graph y = b (1 - (x/a)^n)^(1/n):
    // sqrt(1 + (dy/dx)^2) with dy/dx = -(b/a) (x/a)^(n-1) (1 - (x/a)^n)^(1/n - 1).
    // Bounded and smooth on the segment used below (where (x/a)^n <= 1/2), so the
    // Simpson rule in `SuperEllipseArcSegment` converges cleanly. Precondition:
    // Exponent >= 1 (below 1 the tangent is vertical AT the axis and the graph
    // integrand is unbounded there).
    SuperEllipseArcIntegrand(a: Number, b: Number, n: Number, x: Number): Number
        => (1.0 + ((b / a) * (x / a).Pow(n - 1.0)
                   * (1.0 - (x / a).Pow(n)).Pow(1.0 / n - 1.0)).Square).Sqrt;

    // The arc length of the local-frame superellipse graph from x = 0 to the
    // "half-way" point x = a (1/2)^(1/n) (where (x/a)^n = (y/b)^n = 1/2), by
    // composite Simpson with 96 panels. The split keeps the singular tangent at
    // the far axis OUT of the integration range; the other half of the quarter
    // arc is this same function with the axes swapped.
    SuperEllipseArcSegment(a: Number, b: Number, n: Number): Number
    {
        var h = a * 0.5.Pow(1.0 / n) / 96.0;
        return h / 3.0 * SumOf(97.MapRange(i =>
            (i == 0 || i == 96 ? 1.0 : i % 2 == 1 ? 4.0 : 2.0)
            * SuperEllipseArcIntegrand(a, b, n, i.ToNumber * h)));
    }

    // APPROXIMATE. The superellipse perimeter has NO closed form for general n;
    // this is a numerical arc-length integral: each quarter splits at the diagonal
    // point (x/a)^n = 1/2 into two graph segments (one per axis, the second by
    // symmetry with a and b swapped), each integrated by 96-panel Simpson, times 4.
    // Precondition: Exponent >= 1 (see the integrand). Verified accuracy: n = 2
    // reproduces the ellipse to ~2e-9 relative; ~5e-8 at n = 4, ~6e-7 at n = 8,
    // degrading to ~1e-4 by n = 50 as the shape forms corners.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superellipse
    Perimeter(se: SuperEllipse): Number
        => 4.0 * (SuperEllipseArcSegment(se.SemiAxes.X, se.SemiAxes.Y, se.Exponent)
                + SuperEllipseArcSegment(se.SemiAxes.Y, se.SemiAxes.X, se.Exponent));

    //==
    // # Local-frame and centred-bounds helpers
    //
    // The reduction the rotated planar shapes (Ellipse, SuperEllipse, OrientedBox2D,
    // RegularPolygon) all share: a conversion into the frame rotated by `Rotation` about
    // `Center`, its inverse, and the centred axis-aligned rectangle the bounds bodies
    // are written in terms of. Shared by every section of this library.

    //==
    // # Local-frame helpers
    //
    // The rotated shapes (Ellipse, SuperEllipse, OrientedBox2D, RegularPolygon)
    // all reduce to an axis-aligned test in a frame rotated by `Rotation` about
    // `Center`. These two conversions are the whole of that reduction.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotation_matrix

    // The displacement from `center` to `point`, expressed in the frame rotated by
    // `rotation`: the inverse rotation R(-rotation) applied to (point - center).
    LocalOffset(center: Point2D, rotation: Angle, point: Point2D): Vector2D
    {
        var v = center.Between(point);
        var c = rotation.Cos;
        var s = rotation.Sin;
        return (v.X * c + v.Y * s, v.Y * c - v.X * s);
    }

    // A displacement given in the frame rotated by `rotation`, mapped back to
    // world axes: R(rotation) applied to `local`.
    WorldOffset(rotation: Angle, local: Vector2D): Vector2D
    {
        var c = rotation.Cos;
        var s = rotation.Sin;
        return (local.X * c - local.Y * s, local.X * s + local.Y * c);
    }

    // The axis-aligned rectangle centred on `center` with the given half-extents.
    CenteredBounds(center: Point2D, halfWidth: Number, halfHeight: Number): Bounds2D
        => (Point2D(center.X - halfWidth, center.Y - halfHeight),
            Point2D(center.X + halfWidth, center.Y + halfHeight));
